messages:
ash: FYI found ~0.03% duplicate charges in the canary today after the partition key tweak. small but spikes on rebalance. attaching a brief timeline.
vik: can you summarize the exact window/flow that creates dups?
ash: simplified: producer writes usage-event (local id v1) -> commitlog seq N -> consumer processes -> writes charge. on rebalance, same logical request re-emitted from a different producer instance with a different local id v2 but it has a later commitlog seq M. consumer sees v2 and issues another charge.
tori: so our dedupe key today is local_id which is only unique per producer instance. we need a consistent canonical key.
dave: options I see: (A) canonical key at producer (tenant + root_request_id + schema_version) -> best long-term. (B) consumer-side cross-shard dedupe using a global index (redis) -> low friction but operationally heavy. (C) rely on commitlog seqno + owner-epoch fencing -> bounded but tricky for multi-producer flows.
vik: (A) increases producer API surface & touches a lot of services. (B) adds a hot global lookups path for every event. (C) requires us to emit handoff markers and make consumers epoch-aware.
ash: proposal: hybrid approach. three steps: 1) consumer-only soft-dedupe layer: if we see same logical root within X minutes, flag duplicates and emit "dup_detected" metric but don't block yet. 2) start emitting a canonical token header (opt-in) from new producers (tenant:root_id:v2hash). 3) implement lightweight handoff markers in the commitlog during shard transfers so consumers can reconcile local ids across epochs.
tori: for 1 we can implement Bloom filter + TTL per tenant to avoid full lookup. cheap and gives signal.
dave: handoff marker format idea: FENCE|shard_id|epoch|commitlog_seq_high|wall_ts. Consumers treat FENCE as authoritative: any local ids with epoch < fence.epoch are ignored if they appear after fence.commitlog_seq_high.
ash: example canonical key: tenant_123::req_abcd1234::v2::sha1. e.g., "tenant:123|root:abcd1234|v:2|h:3f2a"
vik: need to think about backfill migration. after we start producing canonical keys, older events still have local ids. dedupe must handle mixed universe.
tori: reconciliation job idea: small offline job that scans last 7 days, groups by canonicalizable fields (tenant+timestamp+payload-fingerprint) and emits compensating-credits when duplicates found. scope it to high-value tenants first.
dave: testplan: failover with synthetic load, dual-producer replay, cross-region skew (clock drift), and a long tail backfill run. integration tests should simulate commitlog handoffs.
ash: rollout plan: implement consumer soft-dedupe + metrics (1 week), opt-in producers to emit canonical header (2 weeks), handoff marker write in leader swap path (2 weeks), reconciliation job + monitor (parallel).
ash: metrics to add: duplicate_charge_rate, soft_dedupe_matches, handoff_marker_lag_ms, canonical_key_emit_pct.
billing-service: flagged. will need reconciliation API to accept compensating credits & a TTL policy.
ops-bot: ticket created: PLAT-4821 (consumer soft-dedupe) & PR#2842. canary schedule: canary-1 -> canary-3 -> 25% -> 100%. ETA ~3 weeks. :rocket:
vik: one more nuance: what if producers synthesize canonical keys differently (hash salt mismatch)? need a canonicalization lib and a version header. keep version in key (v2 above).
tori: agreed. we'll ship a tiny lib in the internal sdk and bump producers gradually.
ash: ok i'll open the design doc with key formats + test matrix. will start consumer PR today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
